message.quantumindustries.vault_landed: §b⚡ A Quantum Vault has crash-landed in a smoking crater near you!
message.quantumindustries.vault_opened: §a✔ Quantum Vault unsealed — Quantum Guidebook received!
This Codex was recovered from the Quantum Vault that fell near your arrival point. Its advanced engineering modules are encrypted (????) and will only be decoded as you demonstrate an understanding of each scientific principle.
This manual does NOT provide crafting recipes. It teaches you how to operate each machine, generator, metallurgical furnace and circuit you discover.

Your first task is to craft the Research Notebook (Tier 1 Research Table) and the Empirical Assay Bench (Material Analyzer). Use them to inspect basic materials (wood, stone and copper), unlock your first studies and reveal this book's ???? chapters.
1. Build the Research Notebook/Table and Material Analyzer. 2. Test samples and complete studies at the table to decode this Codex's ???? chapters automatically.
guidebook.quantumindustries.material_obs: Empirical Assay Bench (Inspection, Impact, Heat and Acid)
The Empirical Assay Bench lets you investigate the physical and chemical properties of 13 basic materials before unlocking new technologies at the Research Table.
There are four test methods: Optical Inspection (Bench Magnifier), Mechanical Impact (Hammer / Brass Weights), Heating (Bellows / Flame Test Kit) and Acid Reaction (Test Flask).
Each empirical discovery can be recorded in the Empirical Field Notebook and provides evidence required by Era I and Era II studies.
Place a mineral sample on the bench and apply the appropriate scientific instrument (Magnifier, Hammer, Bellows/Flame or Flask) to record evidence.
guidebook.quantumindustries.manual_formi: Cold Plastic Deformation and Manual Sheet Rolling
The Forming Bench is the workshop's first metalworking machine. It absorbs controlled blows from the Forming Hammer to turn ingots into rolled sheets.
Malleable metals such as Copper, Iron, Gold, Tin and Zinc can be formed directly on the bench's impact bar.
Hold the Hammer in your main hand and a metal ingot in your offhand (or place it on the bench). Strike the Forming Bench three times to produce one Metal Sheet.
guidebook.quantumindustries.alloy_metall: The Bellows Alloy Kiln reaches higher temperatures than a regular furnace by forcing air into the fire, combining two metals into a structural alloy.

Produces bronze, brass, invar, electrum, constantan and carbon steel. Invar, electrum and constantan require relative heat 160; steel requires 240. One fluorite reduces the requirement by 40 for one complex batch. See JEI for ratios.

Insert charcoal or coal as fuel and the ingredients. For steel made with coal, insert iron first, then two coal; use charcoal as fuel. Operate the Manual Bellows repeatedly to maintain heat. Fluorite is optional for complex alloys and supplies no energy.
guidebook.quantumindustries.mechanical_t: Rotational Torque Transmission and Mechanized Wood Cutting
Mechanical Shafts connect torque sources (such as the Hand Crank or Water Wheel) to workshop machines, including the Mechanical Sawmill and Grain Mill.
The Mechanical Sawmill uses shaft-driven rotating blades to cut logs with a higher yield than manual processing.
Connect Mechanical Shafts to the Mechanical Sawmill or Manual Mill input, drive them with a Crank or Water Wheel, and insert logs/grain at the top of the machine.
guidebook.quantumindustries.hydraulic_po: Continuous Mechanical Torque from Flowing Water
The Primitive Water Wheel converts the potential and kinetic energy of falling water into continuous mechanical rotation, replacing manual cranking.
When correctly placed against flowing water, it drives shaft lines to keep sawmills, crushers and dynamos running continuously.
Place the Water Wheel with water flowing down its side paddles and connect Mechanical Shafts to the central hub to distribute torque.
guidebook.quantumindustries.mineral_bene: Raw Ore Comminution and Doubled Metal Yield (2x Dust)
The Jaw Crusher compresses raw ores between two hard, toothed plates, reducing each raw ore to two purified Mineral Dusts.
This hybrid machine can be driven by mechanical pulses in Era I or supplied continuously with electricity (FE) in Era II, doubling your ingot output.
Insert raw ore into the Jaw Crusher and drive it mechanically or electrically (FE) to produce 2x Mineral Dust, which can be smelted directly into ingots.
Copper Wire and Insulated Copper Wire can be installed on floors, walls and ceilings, automatically connecting in six directions between generators, batteries and machines.
Bare Copper Wire acts as a basic busbar (with thermal losses and a shock risk when energized), while Insulated Copper Wire protects the operator and reduces line losses.
Right-click a block while holding Copper Wire or Insulated Copper Wire to install an electrical network between your generators and machines.
guidebook.quantumindustries.manual_dynam: Converting Mechanical Rotation into Electricity (Forge Energy)
The Manual Dynamo begins the transition to the Electrical Era. Its magnetic rotor spins inside stationary copper coils, inducing a direct electrical current (FE).
With a permanent magnet, no excitation is needed. The crank generates 12 FE per valid action (8-tick cooldown); shaft generation rises to 1.5 FE/t at 12 RPM. 240 FE buffer and 6 UM load.
Operate the Manual Dynamo by right-clicking (or connect mechanical torque) and attach Copper Cables to its output to power accumulators and electrical machines.
guidebook.quantumindustries.scientific_a: Computational Station and Era II: Electricity
The Tier 2 Scientific Analyzer marks the transition from a primitive mechanical workshop to modern electromagnetic engineering.
Equipped with an oscilloscope, crystal lattice display and digital buses, this bench lets you progress between Eras and conduct Era II (Electrical) research.

Build it using deepslate, lapis lazuli, copper sheets and your notebook to take the next step toward electrical automation. At Tier 2, sneak-use an ingot with paper in your off hand to record three relative indices. Review the table in the Knowledge Base. Copper and iron analysis support Industrial Generation.
Install the Tier 2 Scientific Analyzer in your workshop and interact with it to access the cyan panel and research Era II technologies.
guidebook.quantumindustries.galvanic_sto: Electrochemical Energy Storage (FE) and Network Stabilization
The Voltaic Pile and Lead-Acid Accumulator store electricity as chemical potential between copper/zinc or lead plates immersed in an acidic electrolyte.
The Voltaic Pile stores 2,400 FE and transfers up to 48 FE/t; the Lead-Acid Accumulator stores 50,000 FE and transfers up to 256 FE/t. Both are rechargeable on the game's energy scale.
Connect the Accumulator input to generators and its output to machines using Copper Cables. Use Inspection Goggles or Test Probes to monitor the charge in FE.
guidebook.quantumindustries.load_protect: Battery Threshold Control and Mechanical Impact Generation
The Load Relay monitors adjacent accumulators and enables or cuts current/Redstone signals according to configured thresholds, preventing deep discharge.
The Piezoelectric Transducer uses quartz crystals to convert steps, impacts or mechanical pressure into immediate electrical pulses.
Place the Load Relay next to the battery bank to automate generators and consumption lines.
guidebook.quantumindustries.thermal_anne: Metal Heat Treatment and Highly Ductile Heated Ingots
The Annealing Forge (Bellows Brazier) heats iron, copper, bronze, brass and steel ingots to their recrystallization range, relieving internal stresses in the crystal lattice.
Heated ingots resist deformation less strongly and are essential for advanced forming and wire drawing.
Place the Brazier over a heat source (fire, lit campfire, magma, or lava) and insert metal ingots; use the Hand Bellows optionally for a faster blast.
guidebook.quantumindustries.wire_drawing: Die Drawing — Four Wires per Sheet and Noble-Metal Wires
The Bench Wire Drawer pulls metal sheets through calibrated dies of progressively smaller size, producing four conducting wires per sheet without trimming waste.
It efficiently draws not only Copper, but also Gold, Electrum and Constantan for instrumentation and heating coils.
Place a metal sheet in the Bench Wire Drawer and operate the pulling mechanism to draw four calibrated wires per operation.
guidebook.quantumindustries.electromecha: Forge Energy (FE) Powered Stamping and Heavy Rolling
The Electromechanical Press replaces manual work at the Forming Bench with a motorized linear actuator powered by electricity (FE).
It automatically rolls steel, invar, bronze and iron sheets as soon as it receives raw materials and enough electrical energy.
Connect an energized Copper Cable to the Electromechanical Press and feed ingots into the upper chamber to produce metal sheets automatically.
guidebook.quantumindustries.electric_all: Induction Smelting — Steel, Invar, Electrum and Constantan
The Electric Alloy Smelter uses FE-powered induction coils to reach temperatures beyond the Bellows Kiln while maintaining precise component ratios.
It unlocks Era II engineering alloys: Steel (Iron + Coal), Invar (Iron + Nickel), Electrum (Gold + Silver) and Constantan (Copper + Nickel).
Connect electrical power (FE) to the Electric Alloy Smelter and insert the two metal/dust components to synthesize high-purity specialty alloys.
guidebook.quantumindustries.fluid_hydros: Hydrostatics, Fluid Transport (50 mB/t) and Chemical Settling
Copper Pipes and Glass Sight Pipes transport liquids through communicating vessels and pressure, while the Peristaltic Pump moves fluids at 50 mB/t against elevation changes.
The Settling Vat uses gravity and liquid reagents to separate mineral sediments and prepare electrolyte solutions.
Connect tanks and the Settling Vat with Fluid Pipes and install the Peristaltic Pump to transfer water, electrolytes and reagents.
guidebook.quantumindustries.pneumatic_tr: Automated Item Logistics with Air Pulses and Filtering
The Bellows Ejector injects compressed-air pulses that move items rapidly through Pneumatic Tubes between furnaces, crushers and chests.
The Gravitational Sorter automatically separates items in transit by mass and type, organizing production lines without manual intervention.
Install the Bellows Ejector at machine outputs, connect Pneumatic Tubes to the destination and use the Gravitational Sorter to route ores, dusts and ingots.
guidebook.quantumindustries.chemical_lea: Mineral Chemistry — Hydrochloric Acid (HCl) and Phosphate Fertilizer
The vat recipe converts halite brine to HCl reagent as a gameplay abstraction. In real chemistry, dissolving salt in water does not produce hydrochloric acid.
Phosphate fertilizer uses the gameplay recipe with acid reagent, bone meal and sand; it does not represent a real chemical synthesis.
Process Halite in the Settling Vat to obtain HCl and apply Phosphate Fertilizer directly to crops to stimulate immediate growth.

guidebook.quantumindustries.rotation_pri: Uniform rotation, torque, inertia and gears
Angular velocity (ω) measures how fast a shaft turns; RPM counts revolutions per minute. In uniform rotation, ω is constant.
Net torque accelerates a wheel: Στ = I·α. With the same torque, higher inertia I means slower acceleration.
Gears exchange torque for RPM. Doubling output speed ideally halves output torque: gears do not create energy.
Compare the hand crank and water wheel. Use Inspection Goggles to check network connections, capacity and load. These equations are optional deeper reading.

guidebook.quantumindustries.mechanical_t: Cogwheels: the small wheel has 8 teeth and the large wheel 16. Meshing gears reverse rotation. A small driver turns a large follower at half speed with an ideal torque advantage; reversing the pair trades torque for speed. Losses reduce useful output. A closed cycle demanding incompatible ratios or directions jams the network.

The iron flywheel stores work as rotational energy. Its inertia smooths changes in speed, but takes longer to accelerate and continues coasting after the drive stops. Residual motion does not guarantee powered production. A flywheel never supplies free energy.

Pulleys carry rotation between parallel axles using a drive belt. An open belt preserves direction; a crossed belt reverses it. Use Inspection Goggles to read RPM, capacity/load in UM, and the stop reason. Hold Shift for angular motion, torques, inertia, driving power, transmission ratio and network arrows. QKS torque and inertia are simulation units, not calibrated SI measurements.
guidebook.quantumindustries.hydraulic_po: The original 1×1 wheel and the 3×3 and 5×5 rim wheels respond to flowing water. Larger rims can intercept more water, but output follows the wetted rim and its signed tangential flow, not size alone. Opposing flows can cancel. Larger wheels also have more drag and inertia: they accelerate more slowly and need a suitable water arrangement. Minecraft flow is a gameplay input, not a measured discharge or hydraulic head.
guidebook.quantumindustries.rotational_s: Optional physics and mathematics · Era I

Optional deepening: this reference is not a research requirement and unlocks no recipe. Circular motion describes angle θ, angular velocity ω = dθ/dt and angular acceleration α = dω/dt. Angles use radians; ω uses rad/s and α uses rad/s².

Uniform circular motion (MCU) has constant ω and α = 0: θ = θ₀ + ωt. Uniformly accelerated circular motion (MCUV) has constant α: ω = ω₀ + αt and θ = θ₀ + ω₀t + ½αt². These formulas assume constant acceleration; QKS recalculates torque and acceleration as the machine evolves.

Torque τ is the turning effect of a force: τ = r × F. Moment of inertia I measures resistance to angular acceleration and depends on how mass lies around the axis. Newton’s rotational second law is Στ = I·α for fixed inertia: driving torque minus resisting torque and losses determines acceleration, not speed by itself.

Rotational work is W = ∫τ dθ; for constant torque, W = τ·Δθ. Instantaneous mechanical power is P = τ·ω. The goggles show the magnitude of driving torque times measured angular velocity in QKS units. A stopped shaft has zero rotational power even when torque acts on it. UM capacity is a gameplay rating, not N·m.

Rotational kinetic energy is E = ½Iω². A flywheel gains energy only when a source does work, then returns part of that stored energy as it slows. Drag and load dissipate or consume it. Increasing inertia smooths fluctuations but cannot create energy or maintain useful output indefinitely.

For ideal meshing gears, ω₂/ω₁ = -Z₁/Z₂, where Z is the tooth count. The minus sign means opposite rotation. Torque changes inversely with speed so ideal power is conserved; real losses reduce output. Inertia reflected through a ratio scales with its square. Neither gears nor belts multiply energy.

Reading diagnostics: ω and α describe the inspected axle; drive/load/net torque and I_eq describe the simulated reference rotor, while I_local belongs to the inspected part. The transmission ratio maps reference motion to local motion. Stop reasons distinguish source loss, overload, opposing sources, cycle jams and network limits; coasting is motion without powered production.
Optional experiment: compare small/large gears, add a flywheel, then remove the drive. Watch RPM, acceleration and stop reason with Shift. This reference never gates progression.

gui.quantumindustries.hydraulic.rest_leg: At rest: amber ± relative to positive axis
guidebook.quantumindustries.water_moves_: Optional reading · flow, torque and inertia

Water acts on specific sampled regions. The lever arm is the oriented displacement from the axle to a sample. QKS uses τ = (r × F) · axis; F approximates Minecraft flow and is not a force calibrated in newtons.

Positive and negative contributions refer to the positive world axis (+X or +Z). They add and can cancel. Larger wheels normalize samples by radius and perimeter; the primitive wheel limits drive. Goggles report these scaled values in internal QKS units.

Acceleration depends on net network torque and total inertia. A flywheel does not create hydraulic torque: it resists speed changes and can coast after water is removed. Loads and friction explain why local water torque differs from net network torque.

Wear goggles, aim at a wheel and hold Shift. Single blue arrows show sampled flow; double arrows show torque. Green supports current motion and red opposes it. At rest, amber uses the positive world axis as reference. With no effective water, arrows disappear even while the wheel coasts.
Move the water and compare samples, torque sums, RPM and acceleration.

guidebook.quantumindustries.compact_gear: Four mechanical ports connect two perpendicular axes. The gearbox shares network capacity, reverses the sign between axes and introduces small losses. It generates no energy.
The speed ratio has magnitude 1:1. The excluded axis transmits no motion; use Inspection Goggles to verify the network.
Orient the gearbox with the Configuration Wrench. Connect shafts to active ports and power the network with a mechanical source.
guidebook.quantumindustries.mechanical_c: Each segment carries one item. Speed and direction depend on rotation; a blocked output retains the cargo.
Aligned segments share a drive. Chests, barrels, hoppers and compatible machines can supply or receive items, subject to research.
Connect a shaft perpendicular to the belt. Right-click with an item to insert it; crouch and right-click with an empty hand to retrieve cargo.
guidebook.quantumindustries.industrial_c: The switch connects two horizontal terminals when closed. It stores no energy and supports up to 64 FE/t.
In redstone mode, a signal closes the circuit. Opening the switch interrupts only its own path; alternate routes remain available.
Connect cables at both ends. Right-click with an empty hand to toggle; sneak-right-click to switch between manual and redstone control.
guidebook.quantumindustries.electromagne: Industrial generation with excitation and rectification
The field winding requires 24 FE to start. Rotation produces AC, internally rectified; 1 FE/t of gross production sustains excitation. Net output reaches 8 FE/t at 50–60 RPM.
Mechanical load ranges from 2 to 12 UM with production; the buffer holds 1,200 FE. Above 65 RPM it heats up, at 90 RPM it stops generating; thermal protection trips and resets after cooling.

Connect the shaft to the mechanical inlet, a charged battery to the electrical terminal for 24 FE excitation, and tune the transmission for 50–60 RPM. Right-click empty-handed to bind the operator. Sneak-right-click toggles operation.
guidebook.quantumindustries.electric_mot: The motor consumes 24 FE/t and supplies up to 18 UM to the mechanical network. Its internal buffer holds 1,200 FE.
Energy is deducted before torque is supplied. A motor-generator loop loses energy and is not a free source of FE.
Connect power to the electrical terminal and a machine to the opposite shaft. Sneak-right-click with an empty hand to toggle the motor.
guidebook.quantumindustries.steam_boiler: Steam production from water and fuel
The boiler accepts coal or charcoal via pneumatic tube, conveyor or manually. Stores 4,000 mB of water and 2,000 internal steam units.
It converts 10 mB of water into 10 steam units per operating tick. One fuel item supports up to 160 useful ticks. Production pauses without water or space.
Connect a pneumatic tube to a chest (Pull) and the boiler (Push). Supply water by fluid pipes from a tank or renewable source. Use a pump to lift water. Reserve the front for the steam engine.
guidebook.quantumindustries.steam_engine: The engine consumes 10 steam units per tick and supplies up to 24 UM to the QKS network. It does not use FE as fuel.
Steam is supplied directly by an adjacent boiler at the rear inlet. Steam is internal in this version; water pipes do not carry steam.
Align the rear inlet with the boiler's front outlet, connect a shaft to the mechanical output and supply the boiler. Sneak-right-click to toggle operation.
guidebook.quantumindustries.thermoelectr: The Seebeck effect converts temperature differences into FE. Place hot and cold sources on opposite horizontal or vertical faces. Output depends on the gradient, up to 6 FE/t, with a 480 FE buffer.
Magma and fire are valid hot sources; direct lava exceeds the 250 °C limit. Ice and still water heat up and may be consumed. Flowing water renews cooling. Only the best pair generates power.
Try magma on the left and packed ice on the right, or sources above and below. Leave the front output free for a cable and inspect status with an empty hand.

guidebook.quantumindustries.gravity_winc: The winch lifts a counterweight using rotation and can deliver torque as it descends. Free space below limits travel to at most 32 blocks.
It accepts stone, an iron block or a lead sheet/brass weights. Modes are lifting, locked and releasing. Redstone can trigger descent.
Right-click to install a weight, connect a shaft and cycle modes with an empty hand. Sneak-right-click to remove the counterweight.
guidebook.quantumindustries.mainspring_d: Rotation winds the drum's spring up to 100% tension. The spring can be locked or deliver torque, which decreases as it unwinds.
Winding requests 10 UM; release supplies up to 28 UM, with capacity depending on tension. Redstone can trigger release.
Connect a shaft, rotate to charge and right-click with an empty hand to cycle winding, locked and release modes.

research.quantumindustries.heat_transfer: Investigate how temperature differences and materials affect heat transfer.
Enables the study of the Joule Effect.
research.quantumindustries.joule_heating: Combine induction, wire drawing, and heat transfer to apply resistive heating.
gui.quantumindustries.text.era2_thermal_: Apply these principles to annealing and material processing.
gui.quantumindustries.text.era2_integrat: Industrial machines convert energy between motion, electricity, and heat.
Use the Electric Furnace to convert electrical energy into process heat.
gui.quantumindustries.text.era2_electric: Induction enables electrical generation. Cables and batteries distribute and store energy.
Use the network analyzer to compare flow, losses, and connected reserves.
guidebook.quantumindustries.temperature_: Temperature describes a body's thermal state. When two bodies are in contact, heat flows spontaneously from the warmer body to the cooler one.
At thermal equilibrium, the bodies reach the same temperature and net heat transfer stops.
Observe the Electric Furnace chamber during heating and after cutting power.
guidebook.quantumindustries.heat_thermal: Heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference. Thermal capacity describes how much energy is needed to raise a body's temperature.
For the same amount of heat received, a body with greater thermal capacity changes temperature less.
Watch the chamber temperature rise as the furnace stores thermal energy.
guidebook.quantumindustries.first_law_th: The change in internal energy is the heat received minus the work done by the system. The equation ΔU = Q − W uses this sign convention.
In the furnace, electrical energy supplies heating. Processing and heat exchange with the surroundings reduce the thermal reserve.
Cut power during an operation and watch the remaining heat being used.
guidebook.quantumindustries.electric_cha: Like charges repel. Opposite charges attract.
Conductors such as copper allow charges to move easily. Insulators hinder that movement.
Inspect copper at the Empirical Assay Bench to obtain evidence for the Conductivity study.
guidebook.quantumindustries.current_and_: Charge motion and opposition to flow
Electric current measures how much charge passes through a cross section of a conductor per unit of time.
Resistance depends on material and geometry. For wires of the same material, a longer path or a smaller cross section increases resistance.
Use the mechanical assay of copper to study Copper Wire. Later, compare losses on different cable routes.
guidebook.quantumindustries.ohms_law.par: For an ohmic element with constant resistance, the potential difference is given by V = R × I.
At the same voltage, greater resistance reduces current. In series, the resistances of the segments add together.
guidebook.quantumindustries.ohms_law.ope: Compare the losses on two routes using the analyzer. The panel shows in-game energy transfer in FE/t.
guidebook.quantumindustries.electrical_p: Power is the rate of energy transfer. For direct current, P = V × I.
In the game, FE measures energy and FE/t measures transfer per tick. A battery can hold a large reserve and still discharge slowly.
Connect a load and compare flow in FE/t with the energy stored in the equipment.
guidebook.quantumindustries.joule_effect: A resistor dissipates electrical energy as heat. The dissipated power is P = I² × R.
The Electric Furnace heating element applies this principle. The chamber stores thermal energy for processing.
Power the Electric Furnace and observe the chamber heating up before the recipe starts.
guidebook.quantumindustries.energy_conve: A generator converts mechanical work into electrical energy. An electric motor uses electrical energy to produce mechanical work.
Input energy can leave as work, heat, or another form of energy, or remain stored. Each conversion has its own energy balance.
Drive the Hand Dynamo and observe energy accumulating in a connected device.
guidebook.quantumindustries.electric_fur: The Electric Furnace converts FE into chamber heat. A recipe requires material, output space, and suitable thermal conditions.
The chamber retains heat after power is cut. Processing can continue while enough thermal energy remains.
Connect an FE supply, insert a material with a valid recipe, and leave room in the output. Wait for the chamber to heat up.
guidebook.quantumindustries.electrical_n: The analyzer inspects part of the network from the cable connected to its probe. The panel separates injection, delivery, losses, and energy stored in equipment.
Each cable’s flow shows local traffic. The same transfer can pass through several cables.
Place the rear connector against a cable face and right-click to open the panel.
